docs.title: civex db
docs.text:
Database management commands.

Command Description current Show the database's current migration revision and whether it's up to date. migrate Apply any pending migrations now, instead of waiting for the next connect. move Move this project's data to another database. moves List past database moves, newest first. revert Switch back to the database a move came from. setup-docker Set up a Docker-managed PostgreSQL container for this civex project. setup-postgres Configure civex to use a PostgreSQL database. status Show the database's connection, migration, and (if applicable) Docker container status. teardown Stop and remove this project's Docker-managed PostgreSQL container and its data.

docs.title: civex db current
docs.text:
Show the database's current migration revision and whether it's up to date.

Usage

civex db current

docs.title: civex db migrate
docs.text:
Apply any pending migrations now, instead of waiting for the next connect.

Usage

civex db migrate

docs.title: civex db move
docs.text:
Move this project's data to another database.

Copies every record, schema, collection and everything else into the destination, checks the copy against the original, and only then points this project at it. The original database is never changed or removed, so civex db revert can switch back. The destination must be empty or new; nothing is ever overwritten. The same steps apply whichever way you move: SQLite to Docker PostgreSQL, back again, or from one PostgreSQL server to another.

Usage

civex db move [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --to str Where to move the data: sqlite (a new file), docker (this project's Docker PostgreSQL) or postgres (a server you run). Asked if left out. --path str File to create, for --to sqlite. --url str Full connection URL, for --to postgres. Env: CIVEX_DB_URL. --host str Server host, for --to postgres. --port int 5432 Server port, for --to postgres. --database str Database name, for --to postgres. --user str User name, for --to postgres. --password str Password, for --to postgres. Env: CIVEX_DB_PASSWORD. --yes, -y flag false Don't ask for confirmation. --json flag false Print the outcome as JSON, with no progress bar or prompts.

docs.title: civex db moves
docs.text:
List past database moves, newest first.

Usage

civex db moves

docs.title: civex db revert
docs.text:
Switch back to the database a move came from.

Nothing is copied back: records written to the new database since the move stay there. To carry those across too, move again into a fresh destination.

Usage

civex db revert [OPTIONS] MOVE_ID

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description MOVE_ID str yes Id of the move to undo (see civex db moves).

Options

Option Type Default Description --yes, -y flag false Don't ask for confirmation.

docs.title: civex db setup-docker
docs.text:
Set up a Docker-managed PostgreSQL container for this civex project.

Starts (or reuses) a named postgres:16 container, then updates _civex/config.toml with the new URL and creates all tables. The new database starts empty and your data is not copied into it: to carry an existing project's data across, use civex db move --to docker instead. Refuses to switch a project that has records to an empty database.

Usage

civex db setup-docker

docs.title: civex db setup-postgres
docs.text:
Configure civex to use a PostgreSQL database.

Auto-detects a local PostgreSQL server, creates the database and user role if needed, then writes the URL to _civex/config.toml and creates all tables. Pass [bold]--url[/bold] to skip interactive prompts (useful in scripts/CI).

Usage

civex db setup-postgres [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --url str Full PostgreSQL URL — skips all prompts. Example: postgresql+psycopg2://user:pass@host:5432/dbname Env: CIVEX_DB_URL.

docs.title: civex db status
docs.text:
Show the database's connection, migration, and (if applicable) Docker container status.

Usage

civex db status

docs.title: civex db teardown
docs.text:
Stop and remove this project's Docker-managed PostgreSQL container and its data.

civex init / civex db setup-docker create a per-project container that keeps running (--restart unless-stopped) even after the project directory is deleted. Run this before abandoning a project to avoid leaving it behind. Does nothing to a manually-managed PostgreSQL server.

Usage

civex db teardown [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --yes, -y flag false Skip the confirmation prompt

docs.title: civex files
docs.text:
Reach stored files by name and folder, the way the records are arranged

Command Description download Write the selection as one file: a zip of the files and their tables, or, when it is a single table and nothing else, that table. export Build a folder of the files, named and arranged by their records. exports See and clean up the folders civex files export made fetch Download these files from the server, where they are only there. free Free space: remove this computer's copies of these files. gather Move just these files onto one drive. list List the files of some records by the path they would have as folders.

docs.title: civex files download
docs.text:
Write the selection as one file: a zip of the files and their tables, or, when it is a single table and nothing else, that table.

The same paths and tables as civex files export, for taking elsewhere.

Usage

civex files download [OPTIONS] OUTPUT

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description OUTPUT path yes Where to write it: a .zip, or the table's own file

Options

Option Type Default Description --in, -c str Only this collection --schema, -s str Only records of this schema --under, -u str A record (id or prefix): its files and those of everything beneath it. Paths start below it. With --schema, only that schema's records. --field, -f str Only this file field (repeat for several) --where, -w str Filter: field=value (repeatable) --search str Text to find in the records' values --view str A saved view, as schema/view: its filter, its file columns and its layout (--in/--under still narrow it). --export, -e str An export saved with a schema, as schema/name (see civex schema exports): its kind, file fields, filter and layout. Run it in a collection (--in) and/or within a record (--under). --layout str tree: a folder per record above each file (default); grouped: the folders above, but the records holding the files gathered into one folder named for their kind (Encounter/Recording/Selections); flat: every file in one folder. One of: tree, grouped, flat. --table, -t str Also make a table of the records, one per kind of record, named for the kind (Selections.csv). One of: csv, tsv, xlsx, json, jsonl. --column, -C str A column of the table (repeat for several, in order): a field, a ref_field.target_field join, or id/schema/created_at/updated_at. Default: the id and every field. --no-files flag false Make the table alone, without the files. --allow-partial flag false Go ahead without the files that can't be reached (MISSING.txt lists them)

docs.title: civex files export
docs.text:
Build a folder of the files, named and arranged by their records.

With --table FORMAT the folder also holds a table of those records (one per kind, named for it: Selections.csv, or .tsv .xlsx .json .jsonl), whose file columns say where each file is in the folder; --column picks its columns and --no-files makes the table alone.

Prints what can't be reached first. If anything can't (a drive that isn't connected) nothing is made unless you agree, or pass --allow-partial. With --mode link, files spread over more than one drive can't be gathered into one linked folder; use --mode copy --to for those. Running it again on the same folder updates it: new files are added and ones no longer selected are removed. A folder holding other files is refused, so nothing of yours is touched. Remove exports with civex files exports remove.

Usage

civex files export [OPTIONS] [DEST]

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description DEST path no Advanced: a folder to build in (empty, or an earlier export). Leave out to use civex's own exports folder, which civex files exports can list and clean up.

Options

Option Type Default Description --in, -c str Only this collection --schema, -s str Only records of this schema --under, -u str A record (id or prefix): its files and those of everything beneath it. Paths start below it. With --schema, only that schema's records. --field, -f str Only this file field (repeat for several) --where, -w str Filter: field=value (repeatable) --search str Text to find in the records' values --view str A saved view, as schema/view: its filter, its file columns and its layout (--in/--under still narrow it). --export, -e str An export saved with a schema, as schema/name (see civex schema exports): its kind, file fields, filter and layout. Run it in a collection (--in) and/or within a record (--under). --layout str tree: a folder per record above each file (default); grouped: the folders above, but the records holding the files gathered into one folder named for their kind (Encounter/Recording/Selections); flat: every file in one folder. One of: tree, grouped, flat. --table, -t str Also make a table of the records, one per kind of record, named for the kind (Selections.csv). One of: csv, tsv, xlsx, json, jsonl. --column, -C str A column of the table (repeat for several, in order): a field, a ref_field.target_field join, or id/schema/created_at/updated_at. Default: the id and every field. --no-files flag false Make the table alone, without the files. --mode str link link: hard links in a folder on the drive that holds the files, so nothing is copied (refused if the files are on several drives); copy: real copies on one drive (--to). A link is the stored file itself, so don't edit it in place. --to str With --mode copy: the drive (volume name) to copy onto. Default: the project folder. --name str Name of the export folder (default: from the selection) --allow-partial flag false Go ahead without the files that can't be reached (they are listed in MISSING.txt)

Usage

civex files exports COMMAND [ARGS]...

docs.text:

Paths start below it. With --schema, only that schema's records. --field, -f str Only this file field (repeat for several) --where, -w str Filter: field=value (repeatable) --search str Text to find in the records' values --view str A saved view, as schema/view: its filter, its file columns and its layout (--in/--under still narrow it). --name str Only files whose name, or whose record's name, has this

docs.title: civex files free
docs.text:
Free space: remove this computer's copies of these files.

Each comes back when opened or exported. Only files the server confirms it holds are removed, and never one a collection kept on this computer uses (civex sync keep <collection> --opened first). Counts and asks before removing anything.

Usage

civex files free [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --in, -c str Only this collection --schema, -s str Only records of this schema --under, -u str A record (id or prefix): its files and those of everything beneath it. Paths start below it. With --schema, only that schema's records. --field, -f str Only this file field (repeat for several) --where, -w str Filter: field=value (repeatable) --search str Text to find in the records' values --view str A saved view, as schema/view: its filter, its file columns and its layout (--in/--under still narrow it). --on str Only files in this place: a drive's name, 'server' (only on the server), 'missing', 'here' (on a drive that can be read now) or 'unreachable' --name str Only files whose name, or whose record's name, has this --yes, -y flag false Don't ask first.

docs.title: civex files gather
docs.text:
Move just these files onto one drive.

Only the files you select move, not the rest of their collections; pick them by records (the usual options), by place (--on: e.g. everything still on the field SSD) and by name. Files only on the server are downloaded first. It is an ordinary move (checked before the original is removed, safe to stop at any moment, queued behind any other). Use civex files list with the same options first to see what you are selecting.

Usage

civex files gather [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --to str The drive (volume name) to gather the files onto (required) --in, -c str Only this collection --schema, -s str Only records of this schema --under, -u str A record (id or prefix): its files and those of everything beneath it. Paths start below it. With --schema, only that schema's records. --field, -f str Only this file field (repeat for several) --where, -w str Filter: field=value (repeatable) --search str Text to find in the records' values --view str A saved view, as schema/view: its filter, its file columns and its layout (--in/--under still narrow it). --export, -e str An export saved with a schema, as schema/name (see civex schema exports): its kind, file fields, filter and layout. Run it in a collection (--in) and/or within a record (--under). --on str Only files in this place: a drive's name, 'server' (only on the server), 'missing', 'here' (on a drive that can be read now) or 'unreachable' --name str Only files whose name, or whose record's name, has this --dry-run flag false Show what would move and stop.

docs.title: civex files list
docs.text:
List the files of some records by the path they would have as folders.

Shows what can be reached now. A file on a drive that isn't connected is listed with the drive's name instead of a path.

Usage

civex files list [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --in, -c str Only this collection --schema, -s str Only records of this schema --under, -u str A record (id or prefix): its files and those of everything beneath it. Paths start below it. With --schema, only that schema's records. --field, -f str Only this file field (repeat for several) --where, -w str Filter: field=value (repeatable) --search str Text to find in the records' values --view str A saved view, as schema/view: its filter, its file columns and its layout (--in/--under still narrow it). --export, -e str An export saved with a schema, as schema/name (see civex schema exports): its kind, file fields, filter and layout. Run it in a collection (--in) and/or within a record (--under). --layout str tree: a folder per record above each file (default); grouped: the folders above, but the records holding the files gathered into one folder named for their kind (Encounter/Recording/Selections); flat: every file in one folder. One of: tree, grouped, flat. --on str Only files in this place: a drive's name, 'server' (only on the server), 'missing', 'here' (on a drive that can be read now) or 'unreachable' --name str Only files whose name, or whose record's name, has this --paths flag false Print where each reachable file is on disk, one per line, for scripts

docs.title: civex history
docs.text:
See what changed, and when, and undo a change to a record. Entry ids are the short ones listed here.

Command Description collection Show what changed on a collection, newest first. compact Store history written before this version as what changed rather than two whole copies of a thing per edit. The server does this by itself in the background; this does it now, with a progress bar. Each entry is checked to read the same before it is rewritten, and stopping (Ctrl+C) loses nothing: running it again carries on. record Show what changed on a record, newest first. revert Undo a change to a record. schema Show what changed on a schema and its own fields, newest first. show Show one history entry with every change in full.

docs.title: civex history collection
docs.text:
Show what changed on a collection, newest first.

Usage

civex history collection [OPTIONS] NAME

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description NAME str yes Collection name or ID

Options

Option Type Default Description --action, -a str Only entries of this action (create, update, …) --limit, -n int range 20 How many entries to show --offset int range 0 Skip this many entries

docs.title: civex history compact
docs.text:
Store history written before this version as what changed rather than two whole copies of a thing per edit. The server does this by itself in the background; this does it now, with a progress bar. Each entry is checked to read the same before it is rewritten, and stopping (Ctrl+C) loses nothing: running it again carries on.

Usage

civex history compact [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --vacuum flag false Afterwards, give the room this frees back to the disk (SQLite). Needs about the database file's size in free disk while it runs.

docs.title: civex history record
docs.text:
Show what changed on a record, newest first.

Usage

civex history record [OPTIONS] RECORD_ID

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description RECORD_ID str yes Record ID or short prefix

Options

Option Type Default Description --action, -a str Only entries of this action (create, update, …) --limit, -n int range 20 How many entries to show --offset int range 0 Skip this many entries

docs.title: civex history revert
docs.text:
Undo a change to a record.

An update puts the fields it changed back to what they were, a delete restores the record, and a create deletes it. Fields edited since are left alone unless --force is given. The revert is recorded in the record's history like any other edit, so it can be undone too.

Usage

civex history revert [OPTIONS] ENTRY_ID

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description ENTRY_ID str yes History entry ID or short prefix

Options

Option Type Default Description --field, -f str Only put this field back (repeat for several). Default: every field the entry changed --force flag false Also overwrite fields that were edited since the entry --yes, -y flag false Skip confirmation prompt

docs.title: civex retention
docs.text:
Clean up by age: deleted items, change history and workflow runs. Nothing is removed unless you run it.

Command Description forget-purged Delete the history of records that were permanently deleted. run Remove what is older than the retention settings or than dates you give. show Show how long each kind is kept, and what a clean-up would remove now.

docs.title: civex retention forget-purged
docs.text:
Delete the history of records that were permanently deleted.

Permanently deleting a record now deletes every history entry about it. This does the same for records that were permanently deleted before that was so. It cannot be undone.

Usage

civex retention forget-purged [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --yes, -y flag false Skip the confirmation prompt --dry-run flag false Only count

docs.title: civex retention run
docs.text:
Remove what is older than the retention settings or than dates you give.

Give --settings to apply the settings, and/or a date per kind (a date wins over the setting for its kind). It always counts first and asks before removing anything. History about something that can still be restored is never removed. Run civex store gc afterwards to reclaim files nothing refers to any more.

Usage

civex retention run [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --settings flag false Apply the retention settings (each kind left at keep-forever is left alone) --deleted-before str Permanently delete everything deleted before this date --history-before str Remove change history before this date --runs-before str Remove finished workflow runs and their logs before this date --yes, -y flag false Skip the confirmation prompt --dry-run flag false Only say what would be removed

docs.title: civex schema
docs.text:
Manage schemas (data structure definitions)

Command Description add-field Add a field to a schema. add-unique Require a combination of fields to be unique. create Define a new schema. delete Delete a schema (and the records typed by it) to Recently Deleted. exports Exports saved with a schema: which files, how they are laid out lint Report schema and field names that aren't valid slugs. list List all schemas. purge Permanently delete a schema that's already in Recently Deleted. Irreversible. remove-field Remove a field from a schema. remove-unique Remove a uniqueness key (give the same fields it was added with). restore Restore a soft-deleted schema (and the records cascade-deleted with it). restore-field Restore a removed field, with the values records still hold for it. show Inspect a schema's fields (including inherited). unique List a schema's uniqueness keys. update Update a schema's name, label, description, or record name template. update-field Update a field's name, label, required flag, or restrictions.

docs.title: civex schema add-field
docs.text:
Add a field to a schema.

The field name is a slug because workflow steps reference it by name (e.g. civex.get_field's field:). Use --label for the human-readable version shown in the UI and in civex schema show.

Restriction examples: 

--type integer --min 0 --max 100
--type string --choices "left,right,bilateral"
--type string --max-length 255
--type file --accept ".csv,.txt" --max-size 10485760
--type float --unit m --min 0
--type date --precision month
--type geo --geometry-types Point --bbox "-12,48,4,62"

Usage

civex schema add-field [OPTIONS] SCHEMA_NAME FIELD_NAME

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description SCHEMA_NAME str yes Schema to add the field to FIELD_NAME str yes Field name — the machine key used by workflows and CSV headers (lowercase, underscores, e.g. recording_date)

Options

Option Type Default Description --label, -l str Human-facing display name, free text (e.g. 'Recording Date') --type, -t str Field type: integer | float | string | boolean | date | datetime | geo | file | file_list | reference (required) --required, --optional flag --optional Whether the field is required --references str Target schema (--type reference) --min float Minimum value (integer/float) --max float Maximum value (integer/float) --choices str Comma-separated allowed values (string) --max-length int Maximum character length (string) --accept str Allowed extensions e.g. '.csv,.txt' (file/file_list) --max-size int Maximum file size in bytes (file/file_list) --unit str Unit every value is stored in, e.g. m or degC (float). Values are never converted after the fact. --precision str Least precise date accepted: year | month | day (date) --geometry-types str Comma-separated shapes allowed, e.g. Point,Polygon (geo) --bbox str Allowed area as WEST,SOUTH,EAST,NORTH in degrees; west greater than east crosses the 180th meridian (geo)

docs.title: civex schema add-unique
docs.text:
Require a combination of fields to be unique.

No two records of the schema may then hold the same values in all of the given fields, within the same parent record (or the same collection, for a top-level record). A record with a blank in any of them is not constrained. Refused while existing records already share values.

Usage

civex schema add-unique NAME FIELDS...

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description NAME str yes Schema name FIELDS... str yes The fields of the key (the schema's own)

docs.title: civex schema create
docs.text:

The name is a slug because workflow YAML, CSV headers and display fields all reference it as text. Put spaces and capitals in --label instead — that is what the UI and CLI show, and it can be changed freely.

Usage

civex schema create [OPTIONS] NAME

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description NAME str yes Schema name — the machine key used by workflows and CSV headers (lowercase, underscores, e.g. acoustic_recording)

Options

Option Type Default Description --label, -l str Human-facing display name, free text (e.g. 'Acoustic Recording') --description, -d str Schema description --parent, -p str Inherit fields from this schema

Rename with civex schema update --rename / civex schema update-field --rename and move the human-readable text to --label.

docs.title: civex store
docs.text:
Manage file storage volumes

Command Description add Add a new storage volume. adopt Declare that the drive at a volume's path is that volume. collections Show which volumes hold each collection's files. gc Reclaim object-store blobs no longer referenced by any record or workflow job. list List configured volumes and their current usage. move Move stored files between volumes. place Choose which volume a collection's new files go to queue Set the write queue (ordered list of volumes for new file writes). remove Remove a volume from the configuration (does not delete files). set-state Change what a volume may be used for. transfers Look at, pause, resume and cancel moves of files between volumes update Update a volume's path or allocation. where Show which volume each of a record's files is stored on.

docs.title: civex store add
docs.text:
Add a new storage volume.

The path can be on a removable drive or a network drive that is already mounted on this computer. Civex doesn't mount network drives itself: mount it first, then give the mounted folder.

Usage

civex store add [OPTIONS] NAME

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description NAME str yes Volume name

Options

Option Type Default Description --path, -p str Directory path for this volume (required) --allocated-gb float Max GB civex may use (omit for unlimited) --queue flag false Also add the volume to the general write queue.

docs.title: civex store adopt
docs.text:
Declare that the drive at a volume's path is that volume.

A volume is recognised by an identity marker in its root, so civex can tell an unplugged drive from a different drive mounted at the same path. If a volume is reported as the wrong drive but this is in fact the right one (the marker was deleted, or the drive was re-formatted), this rewrites the marker. Nothing else on the drive is changed.

Usage

civex store adopt [OPTIONS] NAME

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description NAME str yes Volume name

Options

Option Type Default Description --yes, -y flag false Skip the confirmation

docs.title: civex store collections
docs.text:
Show which volumes hold each collection's files.

Lists, for each collection, the volumes that hold some of its files with how many files and how much space, and flags files that another collection also uses and volumes that can't be reached right now. Read from the catalog, so it is quick. With --volume it answers the other way round: which collections are on a given drive. To gather a split collection onto one volume, use civex store move --collection.

Usage

civex store collections [OPTIONS] [NAME]

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description NAME str no Show just this collection (default: every collection with files).

Options

Option Type Default Description --volume str Only collections that have files on this volume: what is on a drive.

docs.title: civex store gc
docs.text:
Reclaim object-store blobs no longer referenced by any record or workflow job.

Not a root: audit history and job step logs, which retain FileRef snapshots forever -- treating them as roots would leave almost nothing collectible. Old audit diffs may reference a sha256 that GC has since removed; that's the accepted tradeoff of running this at all.

Defaults to a dry run. Pass --apply to actually delete.

Usage

civex store gc [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --apply flag false Actually delete collectible objects. Without this flag, only reports what would be deleted. --grace-days int 14 Skip unreferenced objects written more recently than this many days, to avoid racing an in-flight upload whose record/job write hasn't committed yet. --show int 20 Max collectible objects to list individually --volume str Only clean up objects stored on this volume (default: every volume). --rebuild-refs flag false Recompute the file-reference table from every record and job before collecting. Normally unnecessary (it is kept current on every write); use it if the table may have drifted, e.g. after editing the database directly.

docs.title: civex store list
docs.text:
List configured volumes and their current usage.

Usage

civex store list

docs.title: civex store move
docs.text:
Move stored files between volumes.

Use --off to empty a volume, or --collection to gather a collection's files onto one volume. Each file is copied and checked before the original is removed, so stopping at any moment, even a power cut, loses nothing. Moves run one at a time: if one is already running, this one is queued behind it. Ctrl+C pauses; resume later with civex store transfers resume.

Usage

civex store move [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --to str Volume to put files on (repeat for several, in order). (required) --off str Empty this volume (repeatable). --collection str Gather this collection's files onto the target (repeatable). --verify-full flag false Read every copy back and check it (slower). --keep-writable flag false Don't make the source read-only while draining. --dry-run flag false Show what would move and stop.

docs.title: civex store place
docs.text:
Choose which volume a collection's new files go to

Usage

civex store place COMMAND [ARGS]...

docs.title: civex store queue
docs.text:
Set the write queue (ordered list of volumes for new file writes).

Usage

civex store queue NAMES...

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description NAMES... str yes Volume names in write priority order

docs.title: civex store remove
docs.text:
Remove a volume from the configuration (does not delete files).

Usage

civex store remove [OPTIONS] NAME

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description NAME str yes Volume name

Options

Option Type Default Description --force flag false Remove even if the volume contains objects (existing file references will become unresolvable)

docs.title: civex store set-state
docs.text:
Change what a volume may be used for.

Usage

civex store set-state NAME STATE

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description NAME str yes Volume name. STATE str yes active, readonly (readable, never written to) or retired.

docs.title: civex store transfers
docs.text:
Look at, pause, resume and cancel moves of files between volumes

Usage

civex store transfers COMMAND [ARGS]...

docs.title: civex store update
docs.text:
Update a volume's path or allocation.

Usage

civex store update [OPTIONS] NAME

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description NAME str yes Volume name

Options

Option Type Default Description --path, -p str New directory path --allocated-gb float New allocation limit in GB --clear-allocation flag false Remove allocation limit

docs.title: civex store where
docs.text:
Show which volume each of a record's files is stored on.

A file is stored once however many records use it, so this is where its content is, not a copy per record. A file on a drive that isn't plugged in is listed with the volume's state.

Usage

civex store where [OPTIONS] RECORD_ID

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description RECORD_ID str yes Record id (a unique prefix is enough)

Options

Option Type Default Description --details flag false Also show each file's path on disk and what else uses it.

docs.title: civex sync
docs.text:
Keep this project in step with an authority: another civex that holds the project's shared copy.

Command Description authority Act as the authority for this project. conflicts List values that did not go in as made, with both sides. connect Point this project at an authority. An empty project becomes a copy of it; a project with data fills an empty authority. Two projects that both hold data are refused. device Devices allowed to follow this authority. disconnect Stop following the authority. The data here stays as it is. fetch Download every file this project's records cite that isn't on this computer yet, now, with a progress bar. Stopping (Ctrl+C) keeps what has arrived; the rest comes later. files See, per collection, how many files are on this computer and how many are not on this computer, and whether it keeps a copy here. With a mode, set the default for collections that haven't their own (civex sync keep). free Free space: remove this computer's copies of a collection's files; they are fetched again when opened or exported. Only files the server confirms it holds are removed, never one another collection kept here uses, and the collection is set to fetch files when opened. interval Set how often the background sync runs. With 'never' it syncs only when you ask (civex sync now, or Sync now in the app). keep Keep a collection's files on this computer: what is missing is downloaded in the background while civex runs (or now, with civex sync fetch). With --opened, fetch them only when opened or exported. library Share workflows and plugins through the authority: publish them from here, install them from there. Nothing arrives by itself. now Send this project's changes and bring in everyone else's. pause Stop syncing until resumed. Changes keep being recorded. reopen Take back 'keep theirs': the conflicts are open again. (Putting your value back, deleting or sending again made an edit; undo that from history instead.) resolve Settle a conflict, or with --all every open one. resume Start syncing again. status Show where this project stands with its authority. user Show or set the author name recorded on changes in this project. It is saved in this project's config.toml; the default is your operating-system user. watch Keep syncing in this terminal until stopped (Ctrl+C): after edits, on the interval, and backing off when the authority can't be reached.

docs.title: civex sync authority
docs.text:
Act as the authority for this project.

Usage

civex sync authority COMMAND [ARGS]...

docs.title: civex sync conflicts
docs.text:
List values that did not go in as made, with both sides.

Usage

civex sync conflicts [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --all flag false Include ones already settled. --record str Only those about this record (its id).

docs.title: civex sync connect
docs.text:
Point this project at an authority. An empty project becomes a copy of it; a project with data fills an empty authority. Two projects that both hold data are refused.

Usage

civex sync connect [OPTIONS] URL

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description URL str yes The authority's address: https://civex.example.com, or ssh://you@lab-machine/~/projects/birds to reach a project on a machine you can SSH into (nothing needs to be running there).

Options

Option Type Default Description --invite str The invite the authority's admin gave. Leave out when this computer has joined that address before (connecting again after a copy stopped part way). Env: CIVEX_SYNC_INVITE.

docs.title: civex sync device
docs.text:
Devices allowed to follow this authority.

Usage

civex sync device COMMAND [ARGS]...

docs.title: civex sync disconnect
docs.text:
Stop following the authority. The data here stays as it is.

Usage

civex sync disconnect

docs.title: civex sync fetch
docs.text:
Download every file this project's records cite that isn't on this computer yet, now, with a progress bar. Stopping (Ctrl+C) keeps what has arrived; the rest comes later.

Usage

civex sync fetch

docs.title: civex sync files
docs.text:
See, per collection, how many files are on this computer and how many are not on this computer, and whether it keeps a copy here. With a mode, set the default for collections that haven't their own (civex sync keep).

Usage

civex sync files [MODE]

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description MODE str no Set the project's default: 'all' keeps a copy of every file, 'opened' fetches a file only when it is opened or exported. Leave out to see where each collection's files are.

docs.title: civex sync free
docs.text:
Free space: remove this computer's copies of a collection's files; they are fetched again when opened or exported. Only files the server confirms it holds are removed, never one another collection kept here uses, and the collection is set to fetch files when opened.

Usage

civex sync free [OPTIONS] COLLECTION

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description COLLECTION str yes The collection, by name or id.

Options

Option Type Default Description --yes, -y flag false Don't ask first.

docs.title: civex sync interval
docs.text:
Set how often the background sync runs. With 'never' it syncs only when you ask (civex sync now, or Sync now in the app).

Usage

civex sync interval VALUE

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description VALUE str yes Seconds between automatic syncs, or 'never'.

docs.title: civex sync keep
docs.text:
Keep a collection's files on this computer: what is missing is downloaded in the background while civex runs (or now, with civex sync fetch). With --opened, fetch them only when opened or exported.

Usage

civex sync keep [OPTIONS] COLLECTION

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description COLLECTION str yes The collection, by name or id.

Options

Option Type Default Description --opened flag false Fetch its files only when opened instead. --reset flag false Follow the project's default again.

docs.title: civex sync library
docs.text:
Share workflows and plugins through the authority: publish them from here, install them from there. Nothing arrives by itself.

Usage

civex sync library COMMAND [ARGS]...

docs.title: civex sync now
docs.text:
Send this project's changes and bring in everyone else's.

Usage

civex sync now

docs.title: civex sync pause
docs.text:
Stop syncing until resumed. Changes keep being recorded.

Usage

civex sync pause

docs.title: civex sync reopen
docs.text:
Take back 'keep theirs': the conflicts are open again. (Putting your value back, deleting or sending again made an edit; undo that from history instead.)

Usage

civex sync reopen CONFLICT_IDS...

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description CONFLICT_IDS... str yes The ids of conflicts settled by keeping theirs.

docs.title: civex sync resolve
docs.text:
Settle a conflict, or with --all every open one.

Usage

civex sync resolve [OPTIONS] [CONFLICT_ID]

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description CONFLICT_ID str no The conflict's id (not with --all).

Options

Option Type Default Description --take str 'theirs' keeps what the authority has; 'mine' puts your value back as a new edit; 'value' puts the one given with --value; 'delete' deletes a record that was deleted there; 'retry' sends a refused change again from the record as it is now; 'restore_above' brings back the deleted records a refused record sits under, then sends it again. (required) --value str With --take value: the value to put in, as JSON (a number, true, a list, "quoted text"), or plain text. --force flag false Put your value back even though the record's value has changed again since the conflict was recorded. --all flag false Settle every open conflict that offers this way (narrow it with --kind), not one. Those that don't, or fail their checks, stay open. --kind str With --all: only this kind (conflict, rejected or edit_vs_delete).

docs.title: civex sync resume
docs.text:
Start syncing again.

Usage

civex sync resume

docs.title: civex sync status

docs.title: civex sync user
docs.text:
Show or set the author name recorded on changes in this project. It is saved in this project's config.toml; the default is your operating-system user.

Usage

civex sync user [OPTIONS] [NAME]

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description NAME str no The name to record on your changes.

Options

Option Type Default Description --reset flag false Go back to the default.

docs.title: civex sync watch
docs.text:
Keep syncing in this terminal until stopped (Ctrl+C): after edits, on the interval, and backing off when the authority can't be reached.

Usage

civex sync watch

docs.title: Top-level commands
docs.text:
Commands invoked directly as civex <command>, grouped the same way civex --help groups them.

Start a working area Description demo Create a demo project pre-populated with example schemas and records. desktop Open civex in a window of its own, with a project picker. init Initialize a new civex project in the given directory. license Print civex's software license. shortcut Put a Desktop shortcut that starts civex for this project and opens it. update Update civex to the latest release. Work on the current change Description doctor Check this civex install and, inside a project, its data. resolve Identify a resource (schema, dataset, or record) by UUID or prefix. Collaborate Description clone Make a new project that is a copy of an authority's, and keep it in step. dump Export all schemas, datasets, records, and workflows to a YAML file. restore Restore schemas, datasets, records, and workflows from a dump file. serve Start the civex HTTP API server. Other Description shell Start an interactive civex shell (no 'civex' prefix needed).

docs.title: civex demo
docs.text:
Create a demo project pre-populated with example schemas and records.

Usage

civex demo [PATH]

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description PATH path no Directory to create the demo project in

Usage

civex desktop

docs.text:
Initialize a new civex project in the given directory.

Usage

civex init [OPTIONS] [PATH]

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description PATH path no Directory to initialize

Options

Option Type Default Description --sqlite flag false Force SQLite instead of Docker PostgreSQL

civex shortcut

docs.title: civex update
docs.text:
Update civex to the latest release.

Detects whether civex was installed with pipx, uv tool or pip and runs the matching upgrade. Other civex serve running from the same copy are stopped first and started again afterwards, after asking.

Pre-releases are only installed with --pre. Once on one, a plain civex update moves on when the final release is out.

Usage

civex update [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --check flag false Only report whether a newer version exists. --pre flag false Include pre-releases (release candidates, betas) when looking for a newer version. --yes, -y flag false Stop other servers running from this copy without asking (they start again afterwards).

docs.title: civex doctor
docs.text:
Check this civex install and, inside a project, its data.

The install checks look for another copy of civex shadowing this one on PATH, for uv, and for a working Python for custom plugins. The project checks look for integrity issues: dangling reference/reference_list values left over from before deletes checked for referrers, and live records that sit under a deleted record (out of sight; civex record restore-above puts one back in place).

With --fix, deletes cached plugin environments that point at a Python that no longer exists (uv rebuilds them the next time the plugin runs).

Usage

civex doctor [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --fix flag false Remove cached plugin environments whose Python is gone.

docs.title: civex resolve
docs.text:
Identify a resource (schema, dataset, or record) by UUID or prefix.

Usage

civex resolve ID

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description ID str yes UUID or UUID prefix to look up

Usage

civex clone [OPTIONS] URL [PATH]

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description URL str yes The authority's address. PATH path no Where to put the copy (default: a new folder here).

Options

Option Type Default Description --invite str The invite the authority's admin gave. Env: CIVEX_SYNC_INVITE. (required)

civex dump [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --output, -o path civex-dump.yaml Destination file --no-data flag false Omit records from the export --no-workflows flag false Omit workflows and plugins from the export

Usage

civex restore [OPTIONS] DUMP_FILE

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description DUMP_FILE path yes Path to a civex-dump.yaml file

Options

Option Type Default Description --yes, -y flag false Skip confirmation prompt

docs.title: civex serve
docs.text:
Start the civex HTTP API server.

Usage

civex serve [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --host str 127.0.0.1 Bind address --port, -p int 8000 Port --reload flag false Auto-reload on code changes (dev mode) --allow-remote flag false Permit binding to a non-loopback address. The server has NO authentication — only use this on a trusted network behind a reverse proxy or firewall. --log-level str INFO Log level: DEBUG | INFO | WARNING | ERROR. Overrides [logging] in config.toml. --open flag false Open the browser once the server is up. If civex is already running on this port, just open the browser. --sync-only flag false Serve only what devices following this project call, for an authority on a network: point the HTTPS proxy at this, and run the app itself on this machine.

docs.title: civex trash
docs.text:
Browse and manage soft-deleted schemas, collections and records (Recently Deleted)

Command Description list List what is in Recently Deleted, newest first. purge-expired Permanently delete everything past the configured retention window.

docs.title: civex trash list
docs.text:
List what is in Recently Deleted, newest first.

This is history filtered to what is deleted now (civex history shows the rest). A delete that took many records with it, such as a bulk delete or a tree, is one line.

Usage

civex trash list [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --kind, -k str Only schemas, fields, collections or records --search, -s str Text to find in a name or a record's values --limit, -n int range 25 How many to show --offset int range 0 Skip this many

docs.title: civex trash purge-expired
docs.text:
Permanently delete everything past the configured retention window.

Usage

civex trash purge-expired [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --yes, -y flag false Skip confirmation prompt

docs.title: civex view
docs.text:
Export saved views

Command Description export Export a saved view's rows, honoring its saved filter/sort and flattening joined columns (text formats use the dotted "ref_field.target_field" header; json nests them). Any file/file_list column is bundled into a zip alongside the table. civex files export --view makes the same thing as a folder.

docs.title: civex view export
docs.text:
Export a saved view's rows, honoring its saved filter/sort and flattening joined columns (text formats use the dotted "ref_field.target_field" header; json nests them). Any file/file_list column is bundled into a zip alongside the table. civex files export --view makes the same thing as a folder.

Usage

civex view export [OPTIONS] SCHEMA_NAME VIEW_NAME

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description SCHEMA_NAME str yes Schema the view belongs to VIEW_NAME str yes View name

Options

Option Type Default Description --format, -f str csv Output format: one of csv, tsv, xlsx, json, jsonl --output, -o path Destination file. Defaults to '.', or '.zip' when the view includes file/file_list columns.

docs.title: civex workflow
docs.text:
Manage and run data processing workflows

Command Description list List all workflow definitions in _civex/workflows/. run Run a workflow against a specific record.

docs.title: civex workflow list
docs.text:
List all workflow definitions in _civex/workflows/.

Usage

civex workflow list

docs.title: civex workflow run
docs.text:
Run a workflow against a specific record.

Declared workflow inputs can be supplied with --input name=value. For inputs of type 'files', value is a glob pattern (e.g. --input files=*.csv). Supplied values are pre-seeded as input. and can be referenced in step inputs like: files: input.files

Usage

civex workflow run [OPTIONS] NAME

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description NAME str yes Workflow name or filename stem

Options

Option Type Default Description --record, -r str Record ID or short prefix (required) --input, -i str Workflow input as name=value. For 'files' inputs, value is a glob pattern.

docs.title: civex.create_records_from_files
docs.text:
Create one child record per file in a file list. No key matching — every file becomes a new record. Reach for this over civex.match_files_to_records when you know none of the files correspond to existing records, e.g. ingesting a batch of new recordings.

Because new records fire record_updated on creation, any record_updated workflow triggered on the new schema's file field runs automatically for each created record.

Plugin ID: civex.create_records_from_files Category: outputs Capabilities: create_record

Config

Field Type Required Default Description schema string yes Name of the schema to create records under. Workflow YAML sets this via the schema: key (the Python field is schema_name). file_field string yes Field on the created records to store each file reference in. dataset string no "" Dataset to create records in. Empty string falls back to the trigger record's own dataset. context_record_id string no "" Parent record ID to attach created records to. Empty string falls back to the workflow's context record.

Inputs

Name Type Required Description files files yes FileRef dicts to create one record from each.

Outputs

Name Type Required Description created number yes Records created. skipped number yes Files whose record failed validation. 
inputs:
  files:
    type: files
    label: Recording files

steps:
  - id: insert
    plugin: civex.create_records_from_files
    config:
      schema: Recording
      file_field: audio_file
    inputs:
      files: __input__.files

docs.title: civex.extract_from_filename
docs.text:
Apply a regex to a file field's filename (or a plain string field) and optionally convert the captured value to a typed output. Reach for this when the data you need — a timestamp, a selection number, a session ID — is embedded in a filename rather than stored as its own field. Works with file, file_list, and string fields.

Plugin ID: civex.extract_from_filename Category: data-access Capabilities: none

Config

Field Type Required Default Description field string yes Field on the trigger record holding the filename to match (a file/file_list field, or a plain string field). pattern string no (.+) Regex applied to the filename. The first capture group (or the whole match if there is none) is extracted. output_type string no string Type to convert the captured text to: string | integer | float | date | datetime. date_format string | null no null Token format for parsing the captured text when output_type is date/datetime, e.g. 'YYYYMMDD-HHmmSS'. Tokens are YYYY MM DD HH mm SS; non-token characters are treated as raw regex, so e.g. 'YYYYMMDD[-_]HHmmSS' matches both dashes and underscores. Required when output_type is date or datetime.

Outputs

Name Type Required Description value any yes The captured text converted to output_type. filename string yes The filename the pattern was applied to. extracted string yes The raw captured text, before conversion.

date_format tokens

Token Matches Example YYYY 4-digit year 2024 MM 2-digit month 03 DD 2-digit day 15 HH 2-digit hour (24h) 09 mm 2-digit minute 30 SS 2-digit second 00

All other characters in the format string are treated as raw regex fragments — not strftime codes. This lets you use [-_] to match either a dash or underscore as a separator:

YYYYMMDD[-_]HHmmSS   →  matches  20240315-093000  and  20240315_093000

Extracted datetimes carry no UTC offset: a timestamp in a filename is wall time where the file was recorded. When the value is saved it is read in the datetime field's timezone restriction, else the collection's timezone, else UTC, and stored as a UTC ISO 8601 string. Set the collection's timezone (civex collection update NAME --timezone America/Chicago) so extracted times land on the right instant.

Examples

Extract a datetime from 20210218_075000_recording.wav: 

- id: extract_time
  plugin: civex.extract_from_filename
  config:
    field: audio_file
    pattern: '(\d{8}[-_]\d{6})'
    output_type: datetime
    date_format: 'YYYYMMDD[-_]HHmmSS'

Extract a selection number from sel_042_contour.csv: 

- id: extract_num
  plugin: civex.extract_from_filename
  config:
    field: contour_file
    pattern: 'sel_(\d+)'
    output_type: integer

docs.title: civex.get_field
docs.text:
Read the value of a field from the trigger record. Reach for this whenever a later step needs the record's current data rather than a value produced earlier in the workflow.

Plugin ID: civex.get_field Category: data-access Capabilities: none

Config

Field Type Required Default Description field string yes Name of the field to read from the trigger record.

Outputs

Name Type Required Description value any yes The field's current value, or null if unset. 
- id: read_audio
  plugin: civex.get_field
  config:
    field: audio_file

docs.title: civex.load_file
docs.text:
Load the bytes and metadata from a file field on the trigger record. Reach for this when a downstream step (built-in or custom) needs the actual file content, not just its reference.

Plugin ID: civex.load_file Category: data-sources Capabilities: get_file

Config

Field Type Required Default Description field string yes Name of the file field on the trigger record to load.

Outputs

Name Type Required Description bytes bytes yes The file's raw contents. filename string yes Original filename. sha256 string yes Content hash of the file. 
- id: load_audio
  plugin: civex.load_file
  config:
    field: audio_file

- id: process
  plugin: my.audio_processor
  inputs:
    bytes: load_audio.bytes
    filename: load_audio.filename

docs.title: civex.load_file_list
docs.text:
Load file refs from a file_list field. Returns the refs as a list without reading the bytes — use civex.load_file if you need the actual content of a single file, or feed the list into civex.match_files_to_records / civex.create_records_from_files.

Plugin ID: civex.load_file_list Category: data-sources Capabilities: none

Config

Field Type Required Default Description field string yes Name of the file_list field on the trigger record to read.

Outputs

Name Type Required Description files files yes FileRef dicts ({sha256, filename, size}). 
- id: get_clips
  plugin: civex.load_file_list
  config:
    field: audio_clips

- id: process
  plugin: civex.match_files_to_records
  inputs:
    files: get_clips.files

docs.title: civex.match_files_to_records
docs.text:
Match each file to an existing child record by extracting a key value from the filename. If a matching record is found, its file field is updated; if not, a new record is created with the key and file field set. Reach for this when files arrive that may correspond to records created by an earlier step (e.g. civex.rows_to_records from a selection table), rather than always creating new records.

Plugin ID: civex.match_files_to_records Category: outputs Capabilities: create_record, update_record, find_records

Config

Field Type Required Default Description schema string yes Name of the child schema to match/create records under. Workflow YAML sets this via the schema: key (the Python field is schema_name). key_field string yes Field on child records to match the extracted key against, e.g. 'selection_number'. file_field string yes Field on child records to set with the matched file reference, e.g. 'contour_file'. pattern string yes Regex with one capture group that extracts the key value from each filename. dataset string no "" Dataset to search and create records in. Empty string falls back to the trigger record's own dataset. parent_record_id string no "" Parent record ID to scope matching and creation to. Empty string falls back to the trigger record's ID.

Inputs

Name Type Required Description files files yes FileRef dicts to match.

Outputs

Name Type Required Description created number yes Records created because no match was found. updated number yes Existing records given a file. unmatched list yes Filenames the pattern missed, or whose record could not be created. ambiguous list yes Files left alone because another file in the same run has the same key (one record holds one file), each with the files it clashes with.

Make the pattern read the whole number

A pattern like sel_([0-9]{2}) reads exactly two digits, so selections 14, 142 and 149 all give the key 14. Use sel_([0-9]+) (any number of digits). When two or more files in one run give the same key, none of them is attached, because a record holds one file and there is no telling which is meant. They are listed in the ambiguous output, each with the files it clashes with, and the run says how many there were.

Note

Numeric captures are normalised (e.g. "042" → "42") before matching so that integer fields match correctly.

Match contour files like sel_042_contour.csv to Selection records with selection_number = 42: 

- id: match_contours
  plugin: civex.match_files_to_records
  config:
    schema: Selection
    key_field: selection_number
    file_field: contour_file
    pattern: 'sel_(\d+)'
  inputs:
    files: __input__.files

docs.title: civex.parse_table
docs.text:
Parse a CSV, TSV or other delimited file's bytes into a pandas DataFrame — the usual first step before civex.rows_to_records or civex.upsert_records.

Requires pandas, which ships with civex. It is imported inside invoke(), not at module load, so this plugin registers quickly and validates without loading pandas.

Plugin ID: civex.parse_table Category: data-sources Capabilities: none

Config

Field Type Required Default Description delimiter string no , Column separator: one character, or a name (comma, tab, semicolon, pipe, space). Used when delimiters isn't set. delimiters array | null no null Several separators the file may use, such as [comma, tab] to read both CSV and TSV files. The one the file's own lines use is picked; a file using none of them is read with the first. Overrides delimiter. encoding string no utf-8 Text encoding to decode the file with.

Inputs

Name Type Required Description bytes bytes yes Raw file contents: CSV, TSV or other delimited text.

Outputs

Name Type Required Description table table yes The parsed rows and columns. 
- id: load
  plugin: civex.load_file
  config:
    field: selection_table

- id: parse
  plugin: civex.parse_table
  inputs:
    bytes: load.bytes

docs.title: Reading CSV and TSV with one step
docs.text:
Give delimiters a list of the separators a file may use, and the step picks the one the file actually uses, from its own lines (fields inside double quotes are ignored). A name such as tab can stand for the character:

- id: parse
  plugin: civex.parse_table
  config:
    delimiters: [comma, tab]
  inputs:
    bytes: load.bytes
  • The separator is chosen from the first lines: the one that splits every line into the same number of fields wins, then the one that appears most, then the one listed first. A file that uses none of them (a single column) is read with the first.
  • Names: comma, tab, semicolon, pipe, space, colon. \t also means tab. Each entry in delimiters must be one character.
  • delimiter (singular) still sets one separator, exactly as before, and accepts the same names. A multi-character value is still passed to pandas, which reads it as a regular expression. delimiters overrides delimiter when both are set.
  • A byte-order mark at the start of a UTF-8 file (common from Excel) is dropped, so it doesn't end up in the first column's name.

docs.title: civex.rows_to_records
docs.text:
Create one new record per table row. Every row produces a new record; use civex.upsert_records instead if you want existing records to be matched and updated rather than duplicated.

Uses pandas, which ships with civex — see civex.parse_table.

Plugin ID: civex.rows_to_records Category: outputs Capabilities: create_record

Config

Field Type Required Default Description schema string yes Name of the schema to create records under. Workflow YAML sets this via the schema: key (the Python field is schema_name). dataset string no "" Dataset to create records in. Empty string falls back to the trigger record's own dataset. field_mapping object no Maps table column names to schema field names. Empty means columns are used as schema field names directly. context_record_id string no "" Parent record ID to attach created records to. Empty string falls back to the workflow's context record.

Inputs

Name Type Required Description table table yes Rows to insert; columns map to schema fields by name unless field_mapping is set.

Outputs

Name Type Required Description created number yes Records created. skipped number yes Rows whose record failed validation. 
- id: parse
  plugin: civex.parse_table
  inputs:
    bytes: load.bytes

- id: create
  plugin: civex.rows_to_records
  config:
    schema: Selection
    dataset: field-season-2024
    field_mapping:
      "Begin Time (s)": start_time
      "End Time (s)": end_time
      "Selection": selection_number
  inputs:
    table: parse.table

docs.title: civex.save_field
docs.text:
Write a single value to a field on the trigger record. Use this to persist the output of an earlier step — for example, a value extracted from a filename or computed by a custom plugin.

Plugin ID: civex.save_field Category: outputs Capabilities: update_record

Config

Field Type Required Default Description field string yes Name of the field on the trigger record to write to.

Inputs

Name Type Required Description value any yes The value to write. 
- id: save_result
  plugin: civex.save_field
  config:
    field: start_time
  inputs:
    value: extract.value

docs.title: civex.save_fields
docs.text:
Write multiple fields at once from a dict, rather than chaining several civex.save_field steps. Reach for this when an earlier step (e.g. a custom plugin) already produces a {field_name: value} mapping.

Plugin ID: civex.save_fields Category: outputs Capabilities: update_record

Inputs

Name Type Required Description updates mapping yes field name → value. Null values are ignored. 
- id: save_all
  plugin: civex.save_fields
  inputs:
    updates: build_dict_step.result

docs.title: civex.upsert_records
docs.text:
Create or update records from a DataFrame, matching existing records by a key field. If a record with the same key exists in the collection, it is updated; otherwise a new record is created. Reach for this over civex.rows_to_records when the same source table gets re-imported over time, e.g. a selection table that grows across a field season.

Uses pandas, which ships with civex — see civex.parse_table.

Plugin ID: civex.upsert_records Category: outputs Capabilities: create_record, update_record, find_records

Config

Field Type Required Default Description schema string yes Name of the schema to create/update records under. Workflow YAML sets this via the schema: key (the Python field is schema_name). key_field string yes Field used to match table rows against existing records. dataset string no "" Dataset to search and create records in. Empty string falls back to the trigger record's own dataset. parent_record_id string no "" Parent record ID to scope matching and creation to. Empty string falls back to the trigger record's ID.

Inputs

Name Type Required Description table table yes Rows to upsert; columns map to schema fields by name.

Outputs

Name Type Required Description created number yes Rows that inserted. updated number yes Rows that matched. skipped number yes Rows whose record failed validation. 
- id: upsert
  plugin: civex.upsert_records
  config:
    schema: Selection
    key_field: selection_number
  inputs:
    table: parse.table

docs.title: What an update keeps
docs.text: An update changes only the columns in the table. Every other field on the matched record (a file, values computed by another workflow) is left exactly as it is, and an empty cell leaves its field alone instead of clearing it. A row whose values are already on the record changes nothing: no history entry, and no workflow triggered. Only a cell with a value is ever written.
